beats.narration: [excited] This drill is cutting a square hole.
[thoughtful] The bit is not a circle. It is called a Reuleaux triangle. Every diameter is the same. No matter which way you measure.

[confident] Start with an equilateral triangle. From each corner sweep one arc. The radius equals the far side. Every arc bulges out that far. Slide a caliper across it. The width never changes. Add the three arc lengths. You get pi times the width.
[warm] Now check your pocket. UK twenty and fifty pence coins. Feel the edges. They are not circles. They are Reuleaux heptagons. Round enough to roll. Triangle by design.
